text:
alex: PD storm on inference-serving — pages from the same alert key blowing up, multiple PD escalations in 2 mins. customers hitting 95th latency SLOs. anyone free to coordinate live mitigation?

devops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0423-003. Notifying oncall. Links: https://redwood.example/incidents/INC-2026-0423-003 :rotating_light:

maria: I can take lead. first step: reduce PD blasts by enabling short-term dedupe + smoothing. propose 5m dedupe window + rate limit 10/min per alert key. Also group alerts by cluster+model to collapse noise.

kevin: +1. Where do I flip the dedupe? Is that in alerting-service or pd-proxy?

maria: alerting-service. temporary flag: `POST /internal/alerts/dedupe?window_seconds=300` on the control plane. or run CLI: 
```
# temp dedupe for incident
redwoodctl alerting set-dedupe --service inference-serving --window 300
```

sophie: I can spin up a quick dashboard showing alert rate by grouping key and top offending models — will add panel to the incident board. link when ready.

jess: I'm on primary PD for the next 30. i'll own the paging flow and customer comms. alex, can you capture customer impact summary? i'll update status page if needed.

alex: customer impact: two customers (acme-corp, beta-app) saw inference latency > 2s for ~10m. some requests timed out. no large data loss, but user-facing slowdown. putting a note in support triage.

maria: action plan (short):
- enable 5m dedupe on alerting-service (temp)
- apply grouping key = `cluster,model_variant,route`
- set PD integration rate limit 10/min per group (via pd-proxy)
- lower severity to P3 for noisy background infra alerts while we stabilise
- dashboard + runbook link posted

kevin: I pushed the CLI change, devops-bot shows `alerting-service.v2` rolled with the dedupe flag.

devops-bot: deploy: alerting-service.v2 -> canary -> prod. status: succeeded :white_check_mark: (refs: deploy/9876)

jess: confirmed PD volume dropped, we're seeing groups instead of 200 separate pages. good improvement.

sophie: dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood/d/incident/inf-2026-0423 — added panels: alerts/min, unique-group-count, top-models.

alex: handoff: jess will stay til 21:30 UTC. maria, can you open a follow-up ticket for tuning? we need durable changes, not just incident flags.

maria: created ticket RW-5557: "Alerting: permanent dedupe & grouping for inference-serving". includes items: longer dedupe windows for noisy alert classes, grouping key review, PD rate-limiter as permanent config, and dashboards+runbook. Pinging infra-sre for SLA review.

kevin: suggestion for permanent rule: use adaptive cooldown — dynamic window based on burstiness. simpler immediate proposal: default 10m cooldown for alerts with >50 events/min in last 2m. will draft in RW-5557.

jess: also let's add a PD routing rule: escalate to pager after 3 unique groups or 5 unique errors within 10m. prevents single-bug fan-out.

maria: agreed. follow-up checklist I'm adding to the ticket:
- create new alert variant with `severity: info` for suspected noise patterns
- update grouping in prod for inference-serving
- add PD rate limiting at pd-proxy (config + tests)
- add runbook section: when to escalate, how to revert dedupe flags

triage-bot: Support ticket created: SUPPORT-1249 linking affected customers and severity notes.

alex: customer comms: support drafted an FYI to acme-corp + beta-app, senior eng oncall cc'd.

jess: leaving a final note before handoff to next shift: dedupe window active (300s), PD rate-limit 10/min set, grouping applied. Will revert to pre-incident settings after 24h if no regressions. :thumbsup:

maria: post-incident follow-up: schedule 1hr review tomorrow to decide on permanent thresholds and automation for adaptive cooldown.

kevin: code note: I'll open PR to make the dedupe window config-driven per-alert-class. link in RW-5557.

devops-bot: Incident INC-2026-0423-003 status: mitigated -> monitoring. autoclose in 72h if no regressions.

alex: thanks all. nice quick coordination. we avoided PD escalation to multiple oncalls. will record this in the incident timeline.

jess: leaving channel, will check in during review meeting. :wave:
